mn116:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Rājagaha on the Isigili mountain.
mn116:1.3: There it was that the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying:
mn116:1.5: “Reverend Sir!” those monks replied to the Fortunate One,
mn116:1.6: and the Fortunate One said this:
mn116:2.1: “Do you see, monks, that mountain called Vebhāra?”
mn116:2.3: “For that mountain Vebhāra, monks, there was once another name, another designation.
mn116:2.4: Do you see, monks, that mountain called Paṇḍava?”
mn116:2.6: “For that mountain Paṇḍava, monks, there was once another name, another designation.
mn116:2.7: Do you see, monks, that mountain called Vepulla?”
mn116:2.9: “For that mountain Vepulla, monks, there was once another name, another designation.
mn116:2.10: Do you see, monks, that mountain called Gijjhakūṭa?”
mn116:2.12: “For that mountain Gijjhakūṭa, monks, there was once another name, another designation.
mn116:2.13: Do you see, monks, this mountain called Isigili?”
mn116:3.1: “For this mountain Isigili, monks, there has been only this name, this designation.
mn116:3.2: Formerly, monks, five hundred Independent Buddhas were settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:3.3: They were seen entering this mountain, but after entering were not seen again.
mn116:3.4: Having seen that the people said this:
mn116:3.5: “This mountain devours these seers - Seer Devourer (Isi-gili),”
mn116:3.7: Monks, I will declare the names of those Independent Buddhas,
mn116:3.8: monks, I will proclaim the names of those Independent Buddhas,
mn116:3.9: monks, I will reveal the names of those Independent Buddhas.
mn116:3.10: Listen to it, apply your minds well, and I will speak.”
mn116:3.11: “Yes, reverend Sir,” those monks, replied to the Fortunate One,
mn116:3.12: and the Fortunate One said this:
mn116:4.1: “One Independent Sambuddha named Ariṭṭha, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.2: One Independent Sambuddha named Upariṭṭha, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.3: One Independent Sambuddha named Tagarasikhī, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.4: One Independent Sambuddha named Yasassī, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.5: One Independent Sambuddha named Sudassana, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.6: One Independent Sambuddha named Piyadassī, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.7: One Independent Sambuddha named Gandhāra, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.8: One Independent Sambuddha named Piṇḍola, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.9: One Independent Sambuddha named Upāsabha, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.10: One Independent Sambuddha named Nīta, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.11: One Independent Sambuddha named Tatha, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.12: One Independent Sambuddha named Sutavā, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:4.13: One Independent Sambuddha named Bhāvitatta, monks, was settled for a long time on this mountain Isigili.
mn116:5.1: Those excellent beings, not troubled, not yearning,
mn116:5.4: please listen as I proclaim their names:
mn116:6.2: also there are Megha, Anīgha, Sudāṭha,
mn116:6.3: Independent Buddhas who have ended what leads to rebirth.
mn116:6.4: Hiṅgu and Hiṅga, ones of great power,
mn116:6.5: the two Jālinas who were sages, and Aṭṭhaka,
mn116:6.6: also Kosala the Buddha, and then Subāhu,
mn116:6.9: Kāla and Upakāla, Vijita, and Jita,
mn116:6.11: Passī, who left off cleaving, the root of suffering,
mn116:6.12: Aparājita, who defeated the strength of Māra,
mn116:6.22: another sage Sayha, who had great fervour,
mn116:6.23: the twelve named Ānanda, Nanda, and Upananda (i.e. 4 to each name),
mn116:6.24: Bhāradvāja, one who bore his last body,
mn116:6.27: Tissa and Upatissa, who cut the bonds of rebirth,
mn116:6.28: Upasīdarī, and Sīdarī, who cut off craving,
mn116:6.30: Usabha, who cut off the net, the root of suffering,
mn116:6.31: Upanīta, who attained the state of peace,
mn116:6.36: the Buddha Kaṇha, whose mind was completely free -
mn116:7.1: these and others who were ones of great power,
mn116:7.2: Independent Buddhas, who had ended what leads to rebirth,
mn116:7.3: these great seers, who had gone beyond the shackle,
mn116:7.4: worship those completely emancipated, who are beyond measure.”
